status: IN PROGRESS — 22 of 46 judged, carried forward into the census-v11 rebuild as PREFILLED BUT UNCONFIRMED. The review ends when all 46 are judged against shipping output and no finding is outstanding.
purpose: Six facets take one value on 90-99% of records. If the RARE value is wrong, most of that class is wrong and the modal value hides it. Only the exceptions can tell you which.
why_halted: The reviewer found a CLASS bug in the first four rows and stopped rather than completing the set. That was correct: the finding changes the extraction, so the remaining 34 rows would have been judged against data about to be replaced. Stopping is not the end of the review — the review ends when all 46 rows are judged against output that will ship.

finding.what: 3 of the 4 `application_language` values were borrowed from a NEIGHBOURING field's enum. The field permits exactly {norwegian_required, english_accepted, unstated}.
finding.smoking_gun: Rows 2 and 3 are near-identical boilerplate from university PhD ads — 'documentation to be considered must be in a Scandinavian language or English' and 'documentation must be available in a Scandinavian language or English'. They received DIFFERENT values, one of them illegal. Same meaning, unstable output: not a judgement call, a defect. Only visible because the exceptions review placed near-identical inputs side by side.
finding.root_cause: census-v7 told the model a documentation clause is NOT a job requirement and never said where it SHOULD go. With no destination, the model recognised the clause and borrowed vocabulary from a neighbouring field — differently on inputs differing only in wording.
finding.why_nothing_caught_it: Tool-use does not enforce declared enums server-side; census_validate checked no enums; scoring checked norwegian_requirement_level alone.

fixes: census_validate validates EVERY enum field, derived from TOOL rather than hand-listed, and demotes an out-of-enum value rather than warning.
census-v9 names application_language's three values, says they are its own, and lists the three borrowed values as invalid.
tests/unit/test_enum_validation.py parametrises over the schema in both directions, plus the cross-field cases specifically.

census-v10 fixes the FEWSHOT, which still contradicted the v9 prose: example 5c showed a documentation clause and labelled it `unstated`, and 5b showed a housing offer and labelled relocation_support `unstated`.
_member() cannot raise: `application_language: ["both"]` aborted the whole census on TypeError, because census.run() does not guard validate().
The repair writes a value each field's own enum permits. It wrote None for evidence_basis and evidence_strength, both required non-nullable strings.
Three enums nested below properties.<field> are now validated: evidence_spans[].section_language, skills[].level, implicit_evidence[].
A required enum field that is None or absent is now an error; a missing norwegian_requirement_level used to raise KeyError inside census.run() after the batch was paid for.
The review page asks TWO questions — is the fact in the ad, and is the value right for the field — because on rows 1, 2 and 4 the honest answers differed.
The page no longer caps evidence at 8 lines or drops lines under 8 characters, and it states how many of the ad's lines matched.
The relocation vocabulary now covers `Hjelp å skaffe`, `leilighet`, `apartment`, `hybel`; row 18's decisive sentence was invisible to it.
An out-of-enum value is marked as such on the page instead of being rendered like a legal one.
pii.scrub gained ad-scoped phone targets: 18 contact phones survived the enumerated pattern in 15 ads, in groupings it did not list.
why_the_verdicts_are_discarded: The reviewer stopped at the finding; 12 of 46 rows is not a completed review and recording it as one would misrepresent it.

THE VERDICT QUESTION WAS AMBIGUOUS for this facet. Rows 1, 2 and 4 were marked 'Justified' — correctly, in that the ad DOES state a documentation language — while the stored VALUE was illegal for the field. 'Does the ad support this fact' and 'is this the right value here' are different questions and the tool offered one button for both.

Row 12 was marked 'wrong' because the tool's per-facet search terms hid the evidence: the ad says 'Ordnede boforhold ved behov' and the filter looked for 'bolig'. Fixed by widening the terms AND by putting the full advertisement behind a toggle on every row, so a filter can never again bound the evidence.
census-v9 changes the extraction, so the 46 exception rows themselves will differ. The review must be regenerated from the census output, not resumed.
next: Regenerate after the full census under census-v9, with the verdict question split into 'is the fact in the ad' and 'is the value legal and correct for this field'.
what_the_pause_bought: Two subagents audited the tool and the fix while the review was paused. Between them they found 10 further defects, 6 in the validator and 4 in the review page itself. Every one would have corrupted the remaining 34 verdicts or the census. This is the argument for pausing rather than pushing through: the 34 unspent verdicts were worth more after the audit than before it.
defects_found_by_audit_in_the_review_too: The line filter capped at 8 matches and dropped lines of 8 characters or fewer, silently. On row 4 that hid the only line naming the application language; on row 22 it hid the bare bullet `Bolig`.
The relocation vocabulary could not see `Hjelp å skaffe leilighet i Bergen` — no `til`, and `leilighet` was absent. Row 18 would have been marked wrong on correct extraction.
Three illegal values were rendered in the same style as legal ones, so the page argued for `justified` on values that are discarded anyway.

The `visa_sponsorship` about text described the FIELD, not the VALUE, inviting `justified` on a weaker test than the enum means. The `conflicting_statements` about text named one scenario the single row of that facet does not match.
A stale closure: a remote snapshot replaced R[n] with a new object and handlers kept writing to the orphan, losing the edit silently.
Ad titles were never glossed, on a page built for a reviewer who does not read Norwegian.

process_incident.what: Commit e31ef0e, made while a subagent was mutation-testing census_validate.py, swept up the agent's in-flight M6 mutant with `git commit -a`. HEAD then shipped a hand-written field list in place of the schema derivation — the exact bug the previous commit was written to prevent — and HEAD's suite was red for one commit.
process_incident.caught_by: The schema-parametrised test DID catch it. The commit just did not run the suite.
rules_now: never `git commit -a` while a subagent holds the working tree
run the suite in the same command as the commit, not before it
never `git checkout --` to undo an uncommitted change you still want — commit the good state first, then mutate

second_finding.found_by: the reviewer, on rows 12-22, with a consistent written reason
second_finding.what: The extractor conflates three different offers under `offered`: (a) accommodation provided BECAUSE OF the job — rotation camps, staff housing, assignment housing for a temp nurse; (b) travel and subsistence WHILE WORKING; and (c) help MOVING there. Only (c) is relocation support. A seeker who needs help relocating and a seeker offered a rotation bunk are being told the same thing.
second_finding.reviewer_note_verbatim: Housing not relocation, travel to work - should be unstated

work travel, NOT relocation: row 13 · dekning av reise og overnatting, betalt reisetid
row 21 · a guaranteed kindergarten place and a page about the municipality
GENUINE relocation support, where the ex: row 14 · Vi hjelper nye arbeidstakere i Norge med å finne bolig

second_finding.assessment: The class is real and 9 of 11 judged rows support it. Two do not: rows 14 and 18 carry an explicit offer to help a new arrival find housing, which is exactly the fact the field is for. Row 18 is also the row whose decisive line the page was hiding at the time it was judged, so the reviewer was working from `Mulighet for rotasjon onshore / offshore` alone.
second_finding.not_fixed_yet: Deliberate. Fixing the prompt now would change the value on most of rows 12-22 and make the carried verdicts about a different value again — the third invalidation of the same review. The order is: finish all 46, collect every finding, fix once, re-extract once, confirm once.

carry_forward.keyed_on: (uuid, field), never row number. `n` is assigned by sorting on (field, uuid), so one row leaving the set shifts every later row by one and a carried verdict would land on a different advertisement while looking entirely normal — putting the reviewer's name on a judgement they never made.
carry_forward.shown_as: prefilled but NOT counted as done until confirmed, per reviews/README.md. Some of these answers were given while the page was hiding evidence, so a carried answer is a starting point, not a result.
